newsitem.title: USA: Judge bars enforcement of Iowa abortion law.
newsitem.headline: Judge bars enforcement of Iowa abortion law.

text.p: A judge Wednesday barred enforcement of a law under which doctors performing an aboriton would in some cases have to notify a close relative of women younger than 18 before terminating a pregnancy.

Judge Ronald Longstaff of the U.S. District Court issued a preliminary injunction that stops enforcement of the law until the matter goes to trial. A number of abortion providers had sued, saying the statute was unconstitutional.
Gov. Terry Branstad urged the state legislature to rewrite the law restricting the notification requirement to parents only, a provision which he said has passed legal tests in other states.
The law requires doctors considering an abortion for anyone aged 18 and under to notify the patient's parents, grandparents, aunt, uncle or adult sibling, depending on who can be reached.
